doc.title: Leslie Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Reaching young children with early jazz
summary: Rowe and Johnson agree that old recordings sound dated but small children respond to the rhythm and can dance to it.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Right. ‘Cause young kids won’t be — I mean I think sometimes the problem with presenting this music is the audio quality of some of the original recordings. It just sounds too different to their ears.
But little kids will not be deterred by that so much.
Um hum. They respond to the rhythm of it.
And they get a kick out of if you play records for them, you know that whole — they’re more easily reached I think.
Well you can dance to it.
